f.title: Treat remote access from abroad and cloud storage abroad as a transfer of personal data abroad
f.statement: A transfer abroad occurs when a controller or processor subject to the Law transmits personal data to, or makes them accessible to, a controller or processor in a third country. Remote access from a third country (even only viewing data on a screen, e.g. for support, troubleshooting or administration) and storage in a cloud located abroad offered by a service provider count as transfers when the three criteria are met, so the Art. 9 transfer rules must be applied to them.
f.clause: 4. Transfer of personal data abroad, A. Definition (second criterion)
f.applicability: Türkiye; KVKK Publication No. 48 'Guide on the Transfer of Personal Data Abroad' (January 2025), explaining Law No. 6698 Art. 9 as amended by Law No. 7499 (in force 1.6.2024) and the Regulation on transfers of 10.07.2024. Applies to a pharma company (data controller or processor) sending personal data abroad, e.g. Turkish ICSRs to a global safety database, PV vendors or licence partners abroad, or giving remote access from abroad.
f.systems: global safety database; cloud hosting abroad
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Partner & vendor oversight; Local PV interfaces

f.title: Without an adequacy decision, transfer only if an appropriate safeguard is in place and data subjects can exercise rights and obtain remedies abroad
f.statement: Where no adequacy decision exists for the destination country, sector or international organisation, the exporter should check whether the parties provide one of the appropriate safeguards (non-treaty agreement between public bodies, Board-approved binding corporate rules, standard contract, or written undertaking with Board permission), provided a KVKK Art. 5/6 condition exists and data subjects can exercise their rights and seek effective legal remedies in the destination country.

f.title: Controller remains responsible when its processor transfers data abroad and must ensure the processor's security measures
f.statement: When a processor transfers personal data abroad, it acts on behalf of and on the instructions of the controller within the purpose and scope set by the controller, and must take all technical and administrative measures for an appropriate level of security. The processor's transfer does not remove the controller's responsibility for complying with the Law and the Regulation and providing the safeguards; the controller is obliged to ensure that the processor takes those measures.

f.statement: Applications to the Board for permission (written undertakings) must state the name, address and signature of the person authorised to apply and attach documents proving signing authority; applications by legal persons must be made by persons authorised to represent and bind the controller or processor, with supporting documents; and applications through an attorney must include the original or a certified copy of the power of attorney. f.title: Group headquartered abroad: appoint a Turkish group member to file the BCR application and accept liability for foreign members
f.statement: If the group's headquarters is in Türkiye, the Application Form and Auxiliary Guide should be completed and submitted by that entity (or another Turkish entity to which data protection responsibilities are delegated, with additional justification). If the headquarters is outside Türkiye, the group should appoint a group entity established in Türkiye, to which data protection responsibilities are delegated, to submit the application on the group's behalf. A Turkish group member should always accept liability where a non-Turkish group member breaches the BCRs.

f.title: Even with approved BCRs, make sure for each transfer that the Art. 9(4) requirements are met and take any additional measures

f.title: Include the minimum provisions (a)-(k) in a written transfer undertaking
f.statement: A written undertaking between the transfer parties must contain provisions on, in particular: (a) purpose, scope, nature and legal basis of the transfer; (b) definitions consistent with the Law; (c) commitment to the general principles of KVKK Art. 4; (ç) how data subjects are informed of the undertaking and the transfer; (d) commitment to enable data subjects' Art. 11 rights and the request procedure; (e) commitment to all technical and administrative measures for appropriate security; (f) commitment to the adequate measures set by the Board for special categories of data; (g) restrictions on onward transfers; (ğ) remedies for data subjects if the undertaking is breached; (h) the recipient's commitment to comply with Board decisions and opinions; (ı) the recipient's statement that no national rule prevents compliance and that it will notify the exporter as soon as possible of a likely change, with the exporter's right to suspend and terminate; (i) the exporter's right to suspend and terminate if the recipient cannot comply; (j) return of the data with backups or their complete destruction on termination, at the exporter's choice; and (k) Turkish law and the jurisdiction of Turkish courts.

f.title: Use exceptional (derogation) transfers only incidentally, as a last resort, in the exhaustive Art. 9(6) cases
f.statement: Where there is no adequacy decision and none of the appropriate safeguards can be provided, data controllers and processors may transfer personal data abroad only incidentally (one-off or a few times, not continuous, outside the ordinary course of business) and only in one of the exhaustively listed cases: explicit consent after being informed of possible risks; necessity for a contract with the data subject or pre-contractual measures at their request; necessity for a contract in the data subject's interest; overriding public interest; establishment, exercise or defence of a right; protection of the life or physical integrity of a person unable to consent; or transfer from a public register. These exceptions should be interpreted very narrowly and used as a last resort after checking adequacy and safeguards. No Board permission or notification is required for incidental transfers.

f.title: Before consent-based transfers, inform data subjects of the exporter, purpose, data, withdrawal right, lack of adequacy and the possible risks
f.statement: For consent to an exceptional transfer, the data subject must be informed before the transfer of, among other things, the identity of the exporter, the purpose of the transfer, the type of data transferred and the right to withdraw consent; the information should also state that consent is the legal ground for the transfer and that there is no Board adequacy decision for the destination country. In addition, data subjects must be informed of the possible risks arising from the transfer (e.g. that there may be no supervisory authority or that data protection principles or rights may not be ensured in the destination country).
f.clause: 7. B. I. Explicit consent, b. Based on information
f.applicability: Türkiye; KVKK Publication No. 48 'Guide on the Transfer of Personal Data Abroad' (January 2025), explaining Law No. 6698 Art. 9 as amended by Law No. 7499 (in force 1.6.2024) and the Regulation on transfers of 10.07.2024. Applies to a pharma company (data controller or processor) sending personal data abroad, e.g. Turkish ICSRs to a global safety database, PV vendors or licence partners abroad, or giving remote access from abroad.
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Safety intake & collection

rows.actor: Data exporter (data controller)
rows.quote:
Bilgilendirme veri aktaranın kimliği,
aktarımın amacı, aktarılan kişisel verilerin türü, açık rızayı geri
alma hakkının varlığı gibi konuları içerir. Bilgilendirme açık
rızanın aktarım için yasal bir gerekçe olduğunu ve verilerin
aktarılacağı ülke hakkında Kurul tarafından alınmış bir yeterlilik
kararı olmadığını da içermelidir. Bilgilendirme aktarımdan önce
yapılmalıdır. Genel olarak yapılan bilgilendirmeye ek olarak,
kişisel verilerin yurt dışına aktarıldığı durumlarda ilgili kişilerin
aktarım dolayısıyla oluşabilecek muhtemel riskler hakkında da
bilgilendirilmesi gerekir.
rows.location: 7. B. I. Explicit consent, b. Based on information
rows.review_note: Review: mixed modals: risk information 'bilgilendirilmesi gerekir' (must) is the headline legal condition of Art. 9(6)(a), so Mandatory; the lack-of-adequacy and before-transfer points use '-meli' (should). Risk examples from sub-section c. Translation check: agrees. Double-check: mixed-modal row, level follows the statutory risk-information condition; 88.
rows.quote_en: The information includes matters such as the identity of the data exporter, the purpose of the transfer, the type of personal data transferred and the existence of the right to withdraw explicit consent. The information should also include that explicit consent is a legal ground for the transfer and that there is no adequacy decision taken by the Board for the country to which the data will be transferred. The information should be given before the transfer. In addition to the general information, where personal data are transferred abroad, data subjects must also be informed of the possible risks that may arise from the transfer.

f.title: Vital-interest exceptional transfer only for a person unable to consent, e.g. a medical emergency, not for general research
f.statement: Personal data may be transferred abroad where necessary to protect the life or physical integrity of the data subject or another person who cannot give consent due to actual impossibility or whose consent is not legally valid. This may apply in a medical emergency where the transfer of certain data is necessary to provide medical care (e.g. sending health records to a person abroad who will intervene); the inability to consent must be demonstrable, and a balancing test is required. It cannot be used for general research beyond protecting life or physical integrity.
f.clause: 7. B. VI. Protection of life or physical integrity of a person unable to consent
f.applicability: Türkiye; KVKK Publication No. 48 'Guide on the Transfer of Personal Data Abroad' (January 2025), explaining Law No. 6698 Art. 9 as amended by Law No. 7499 (in force 1.6.2024) and the Regulation on transfers of 10.07.2024. Applies to a pharma company (data controller or processor) sending personal data abroad, e.g. Turkish ICSRs to a global safety database, PV vendors or licence partners abroad, or giving remote access from abroad.
f.exceptions: Not applicable where the data subject can give valid consent, nor for general research beyond protecting life or physical integrity.
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Medical review

rows.quote_en: [This incidental case] may apply [where there is a medical emergency and] in situations where the transfer of certain personal data is necessary in order for medical care to be provided. For example, the transfer of health records to a person abroad who will intervene in relation to the health condition may be considered in this scope.

f.title: Transfers that would seriously harm Türkiye's or the data subject's interests need Board permission after the opinion of the relevant public body
f.statement: Subject to international agreements, where the interests of Türkiye or of the data subject would be seriously harmed, personal data may be transferred abroad only with the permission of the Board after obtaining the opinion of the relevant public institution; this applies even to incidental transfers that otherwise need no permission or notification.
f.clause: 7. Third tier: exceptional transfers (no permission or notification for incidental transfers)
f.applicability: Türkiye; KVKK Publication No. 48 'Guide on the Transfer of Personal Data Abroad' (January 2025), explaining Law No. 6698 Art. 9 as amended by Law No. 7499 (in force 1.6.2024) and the Regulation on transfers of 10.07.2024. Applies to a pharma company (data controller or processor) sending personal data abroad, e.g. Turkish ICSRs to a global safety database, PV vendors or licence partners abroad, or giving remote access from abroad.
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Partner & vendor oversight; Local PV interfaces

rows.quote_en: However, it should not be forgotten that, where the interests of Türkiye or of the data subject would be seriously harmed, personal data may be transferred abroad, without prejudice to the provisions of international agreements, only with the permission of the Board after obtaining the opinion of the relevant public institution or body (KVKK Art. 9(9)).
